answer: To join, an agent escrows a bond paid in umber-assay credits—a pigment whose remaining stock is publicly inventoried and cannot be minted. A verifier then issues a one-time whisper nonce that the claimant's scarce hardware root must sign inside a twelve-second horizon. Acceptance requires both a matching registered root and a timely signature; a failed check slashes the bond. Each fake identity therefore costs another credit, another root module, and the full escrow, so attacker spend grows linearly with every extra ID.
